prompt: The point $(\cos 300^\circ,\ \sin 300^\circ)$ lies in which quadrant?

choices.label: Quadrant I, where both coordinates are positive
Quadrant III, where both coordinates are negative

hint: $300^\circ$ is between $270^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ — almost all the way around.

hints.text: $300^\circ$ is between $270^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ — almost all the way around.
That last stretch of the circle is below the $x$-axis and to the right of the $y$-axis.
It is Quadrant IV: $\cos 300^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$ is positive and $\sin 300^\circ = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ is negative.

explanation: Angles from $270^\circ$ to $360^\circ$ sweep through the final quarter of the circle, which is Quadrant IV.
There the points are to the right of the $y$-axis (positive $x$) and below the $x$-axis (negative $y$).
Indeed $\cos 300^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$ and $\sin 300^\circ = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, matching a positive $x$ and negative $y$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count backwards from a full turn
steps: $300^\circ$ is $60^\circ$ short of a full $360^\circ$ turn.
So the point sits $60^\circ$ below the starting ray — down and to the right, which is Quadrant IV.
